highlights.description: `respell` turns IPA and dictionary respellings, as Wikipedia writes them, into respellings a plain-text speech engine reads as intended
Several candidate respellings per word to play and choose from, since voices read unfamiliar words by their own rules

added.description: `FromIPA` reads IPA into syllables with stress: stress marks and breaks start syllables, the longest legal English onset goes to the next syllable, affricates and diphthongs are joined, doubled consonants collapsed
`Word.Respelling` writes syllables in the style of Wikipedia's pronunciation respelling key, stressed syllables in capitals, as in LAM-bər-GHEE-nee
IPA in other languages (Italian, Spanish, French, German and more) brought to the nearest English sounds: pure vowels written long, nasal vowels with an n
`FromRespelling` reads a hyphenated respelling such as LAM-bər-GHEE-nee back into syllables
`Candidates` writes a word's sounds up to `MaxCandidates` ways: as one word, split where the stress falls, syllable by syllable, with simpler endings and with a consonant cluster split
`Suggest` reads text as Wikipedia writes it: English IPA between slashes, bracketed IPA in the language named before it (`Languages`), and hyphenated respellings, returning a `Suggestion` per word

tests.description: Tests for IPA syllables, respellings, candidates and Wikipedia text in several languages
